# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 92 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 92 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_092_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — The Plain Explained

**1** "What about the stones brought from the plain that were fitted into the tower to replace the rejected ones?" I asked. **2** "They come from the roots of the white mountain," he said. "Since everyone from the white mountain had proven to be innocent, the lord of the tower ordered these stones from the mountain's roots to be brought in so the tower could be finished. **3** He knew that placed in the building, these stones would stay bright and none of them would turn dark the way stones from the other mountains had. **4** Since the tower needed to be completed, the lord ordered them brought immediately and set into place." **5** "What does the plain represent?" I asked. "And the other mountains?" **6** "All the mountains and the plain together," he said, "represent one world. **7** That is why the lord called all these peoples — from across the whole world — to bring stones for the tower's construction. **8** And that's why the white stones from the plain are in the same category as those from the white mountain — they share the same inner character. The only difference is that the plain-stones were drawn directly from the world." **9** "But so many stones were rejected and didn't fit — why? How many were rejected in total?" **10** "The round ones," he said, "are the wealthy who are attached to the world; when trouble comes and they hear about it, they abandon their Lord." **11** "And the rough ones?" **12** "These are people who encountered the truth but didn't stay with it. They drifted away from the community of believers, and the recklessness and skepticism inside them made them rough — so they were thrown out."

---

*PNEUMA renders the plain/world identification and the stone-type typology in plain contemporary terms, making the pastoral diagnosis accessible.*
